# Welcome {-}

> This is a **fork** from [tidyverse's guide](https://github.com/tidyverse/style) and has been adapted where needed for the Gaiti Lab.

Good coding style is like correct punctuation: you can manage without it, butitsuremakesthingseasiertoread. This site describes the style used in the Gaiti Lab.

All style guides are fundamentally opinionated. Some decisions genuinely do make code easier to use (especially matching indenting to programming structure), but many decisions are arbitrary. The most important thing about a style guide is that it provides consistency, making code easier to write because you need to make fewer decisions.

> This is a public repo and covers best practices for R, file naming conventions and git, for (additional) **internal** documentation see [GaitiLab/GaitiLabToolBox](https://github.com/GaitiLab/GaitiLabToolBox/tree/main/docs) (private repo).

R packages/extensions support this style guide:

*   [styler](http://styler.r-lib.org) allows you to interactively restyle
    selected text, files, or entire projects. It includes an RStudio add-in,
    the easiest way to re-style existing code.

    ```{r}
    #| eval: true
    #| echo: false
    #| fig-align: center
    knitr::include_graphics("styler-addin.png", dpi = 220)
    ```

*   [lintr](https://github.com/r-lib/lintr) performs automated checks
    to confirm that you conform to the style guide.

*   [air](https://posit-dev.github.io/air/) allows you to interactively restyle/format
    selected text, files, or entire projects.
